G10.title: Profile menus and the duplicate client cabinet
G10.why: S-048 and S-111 are one compiled profile sheet shipped in two bundles — `app.html` and `maya-os-site/index.html`, the same four rows and role branch — not two menus; S-111 is a tab with no screen, duplicating the «Кабинет» tab beside it. S-176 differs in kind: an independent client cabinet inside the marketing page calling the same production endpoints, so retiring it removes a duplicate client app, and two remain.
G10.disappear: The profile sheet in both bundles, the 4th tab that exists only to open it, and the marketing overlay as a separate client codebase, with its `?cab_demo=` QA harness. Body re-parenting goes only after the unclosed `#promo-overlay` is fixed — removed earlier, the merged surface renders invisible.
G10.remain: Everything these rows front: cabinet entry, settings, logout, and the client's own points, visits and history behind the same authenticated endpoints, with one of three implementations removed. Theme too — but the successor should better it, not copy it: today's toggle deliberately does not persist and reverts itself every five minutes.
G10.user_impact: Two populations, one component: the client's 4th tab and the staff avatar open the same sheet. One loss is verified and material — the settings screen has exactly one route, and losing it leaves a client holding a consent record with no live control over what is sent. The logout loss applies only to non-business clients; theme is a gain, since today's toggle does not stick.
G10.security_impact: Neutral for authority — nothing closed, nothing opened. The role branch picks a destination, not a gate, but the inference that those screens enforce their own access is unevidenced: resolve the destination server-side and confirm its data endpoints authorize independently before dropping the branch. Consolidation is miscounted — the endpoints are called from three bundles, and only the marketing overlay retires.
G10.risk: MEDIUM — one loss is unambiguous, the rest narrower. `__meGo('settings')` occurs exactly once and is the only route to the settings screen — reminder timing, notification switches. Lose that row unreplaced and a client keeps a consent record with no live control over what is sent, the one loss touching 152-ФЗ. All three are RETIRE AFTER PARITY: a parity hazard, not a live one.
G10.dropped: The site's RU/EN bilingual re-render (12 `setLanguage` hooks in index.html, none in the PWA) — a site-language contract must exist before the site entry retires — and the no-`fetch` fallback to `/app/`, today the only graceful degradation.
